alia: Quick heads up — PR #9875 (private install quickstart) landed but the VPC networking examples section is missing the dual-homed gateway note. Can someone pick this up?
chris: I skimmed it, saw the SNAT vs MASQUERADE callout is gone too. I can add a brief example, but need consensus on the recommended nat rule for sealed networks.
rafael: For sealed sites we prefer explicit SNAT and sticky source, otherwise kube-proxy healthchecks bounce. Example we use: `iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.100.0.0/16 -j SNAT --to-source 203.0.113.12`
monica: +1 for SNAT in the docs. Also we should add a note about ip_forward and rp_filter settings — folks forget sysctl on airgapped nodes.
alia: Great — can you add both the rule and the sysctl snippet, @monica? Keep it short.
monica: On it. Draft below, please sanity check: ```
# enable forwarding
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward
# loosen rp_filter for multi-homed hosts
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter
```
chris: Looks good. Add a one-liner about persistence (sysctl -w vs /etc/sysctl.d/99-redwood.conf).
monica: Will do. Also noticed the KMS section references an internal runbook link that 404s — "redwood.internal/kms-runbook". @rafael do you have the public/how-to snippet we can link instead?
rafael: The public fragment is in the ops repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/blob/main/kms/README.md#onprem-quickstart — use that. I'll paste a short example for PKCS#11 binding.
rafael: PKCS#11 mount example (add to docs under HSM notes): ```
# mount token (example)
pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/pkcs11/softhsm2.so -l -y 0
# configure engine (pseudo)
openssl engine -t pkcs11 -pre SO_PIN:1234
```
alia: Perfect. One more: the SDK code snippet for connection string in private deploy is out of date (uses `api.redwood.ai`), needs to show VPC internal endpoint pattern. @chris can you update the snippet to include an env var example?
chris: Yep. Proposed snippet: ```
# prefer env var for endpoint in private deploy
export REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=https://internal-redwood.<customer-vpc>.svc.cluster.local
python -c "import os, redwood; c=redwood.Client(endpoint=os.getenv('REDWOOD_ENDPOINT'))"
```
monica: I also added a tiny troubleshooting note: if the SDK fails TLS, confirm the cluster CA is in the container trust store and the endpoint matches SANs.
doc-bot: Automated check: PR #9875 missing link: https://redwood-internal/ops/kms-runbook — flagged.
alia: Thanks. Action items: @monica add sysctl + persistence note, @chris update SDK endpoint snippet and nat example, @rafael paste final PKCS11 snippet and public link. I'll review and merge.
chris: I pushed change to the branch with NAT + SDK snippet. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/9875/files
rafael: PKCS#11 snippet added and link updated.
monica: Done — added sysctl persistence and a short troubleshooting bullet.
alia: LGTM. I'll run quick link check and merge if green.
alia: Merge done, deploy preview requested. :shipit:
